dispositionOfTheHybridVintage: FIXED (not just diagnosed). Root cause: applyEnvelopeSetbackOverride can fold a same-day parcel_record axis override onto an older atom-chain envelope, but the response's top-level snapshotAt/facets.bakedAt were never bumped to reflect it -- composeSetbackAxisScalar discarded each overridden cell's own `vintage` entirely. Fix: composeSetbackAxisScalarWithVintage threads the vintage through; composeZoningSetbackOverride surfaces the latest one as setbackAxisOverrideVintage; applyRecordPatch takes the newer of that and the existing snapshotAt (and mirrors it onto facets.bakedAt), gated on an override having actually happened so an untouched payload is never touched. New tests (pe-property-atoms.test.ts) prove both the bump (using the dispatch's own 2026-07-23/2026-09-15 dates) and the no-op case. Note: P-214's own CP1 (same OPS-24 wave, this same repo) independently found a RELATED but DISTINCT staleness divergence on a different parcel (48021:8723767: two entirely different serving routes -- /api/spine/property-atoms/.../facets vs get_smart_site -- disagreed on bakedAt by 32 days, root cause of the 32-day gap itself not traced). This fix addresses the axis-override mechanism specifically; it does not establish whether it also explains P-214's 32-day divergence, which remains open (see leave_behind).
whatWasDoneAboutTheUnreadableDateBasis: NOT fixed; precisely diagnosed and left as leave_behind, deliberately not attempted as a code change this pass. The 35,365 parcel_record_cell rows come from hauska-factory's factory-parcel-setback-cells bulk classification job (parcel-setback-cells.mjs), which reads exactly ONE setback-corpus row per jurisdiction (keyed on zoningDistrict) and writes it as a 'value' cell -- a structurally different, simpler write path than legacy-design-tools' authoritativeSetbackSource.ts, which already implements the 2026-09-11 ruling's conflict mechanism (resolveMostCurrentSetback / a disclosed `conflict` field) for ITS OWN live atom-chain-vs-codified-table reconciliation. Established with evidence, not assumed: the bulk writer has no second dated candidate to disagree with at write time, so 'conflict row' in the strict sense the ruling's own resolver implements (two-or-more dated candidates disagreeing) does not obviously apply to these 35,365 rows viewed in isolation -- there is nothing to conflict against. What remains genuinely open and NOT established either way: whether these bulk-written corpus values silently diverge from whatever hauska-engine's own atom-chain independently computes for the SAME parcels, which would be a real cross-system R-1 violation of exactly the kind the ruling exists to prevent (this pattern -- two systems producing different numbers for the same parcel, neither citing the other -- is literally how the 2026-09-11 ruling's own 'Context' section describes the 48021:34049 incident that prompted it). Checking this at 35,365-row scale requires direct queries against both hauska-factory's parcel_record_cell store and hauska-engine's retrieval-api/atom-chain store; this session holds credentials for neither, and a same-day sibling close (P-200) explicitly warned against ad hoc heavy scans against the same production store under load. A backfill write to raise conflict rows, if one is genuinely warranted, is also a write to a production serving store -- one of OPS-24's three explicit operator stop-points regardless of which repo it lands in, and not something to attempt inline in a route-composer PR.
